newsitem.title: SPAIN: Via Digital offers new Spain pay-TV package.
newsitem.headline: Via Digital offers new Spain pay-TV package.

text.p: Via Digital of Spain presented a 35-channel basic pay television package at a media preview on Tuesday, but it still faced problems in securing crucial soccer viewing rights and some of its financial partners are caught up in shifting alliances.

Pedro Perez, chairman of the Telefonica-led digital television platform, said he was confident the group's pay-TV offer was competitive and would include Spanish soccer matches. But he said a final deal had not been made.

"With this basic package, Via Digital becomes the most ample and competitive offer in Spanish pay television," Perez told a news conference. "We hope to count on first division soccer from the start of the season."
Rival digital platform CanalSatelite, backed by French pay-TV operator Canal Plus, currently holds exclusive rights to televise Spain's champion league soccer matches.
The soccer rights, which industry analysts say are critical to make the investment-heavy platforms profitable, have bounced back and forth between the two groups.
Perez said there was room for both platforms to air soccer games and insisted Via Digital would provide coverage.

"We will have soccer in pay for view," he said, adding that Via Digital had offered 130 billion pesetas ($844 million) to share the soccer rights, more than eight times the amount CanalSatelite had paid.

Last week, Telefonica teamed up with television channel Antena 3 to acquire its 40 percent stake in GMA, which owns the soccer rights. Perez said Antena 3, which had a preliminary deal with the Telefonica group before defecting to CanalSatelite late last year, would work closely with Via Digital but would not become a formal partner.
Other backers of the Via Digital project, the platform favoured by Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar's conservative government, are in the midst of shifting alliances.

Perez said both Spanish state television RTVE and Mexico's Televisa are to cut their stakes from 25 percent to 17 percent each next week. Telefonica will reduce its 35 percent participation to the legal limit for television channels or platforms of 25 percent.
Last week, the Recoletos publishing group said it wanted to sell its five percent Via Digital stake.
Perez said Catalan television channel TV3, which is also part of GMA, would take a five percent participation as would Japan's Itochu Corporation.

Meanwhile, Via Digital is working feverishly to put together its basic package in time for a September launch, Perez said. The platform will offer 35 television and 30 audio channels for less than 2,500 pesetas per month.

It will include a new 24-hour news programme in Spanish put out by RTVE as well as three 24-hour film channels. There are also channels for sports, cartoons, travel, education, financial news, soap operas, an interactive internet channel and nationwide access to regional television stations broadcast in the local languages.
Via Digital is also negotiating rights to show newly released films on a pay-per-view basis.
